implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.py defines GRID_SIZE = 3 and gui.draw_board iterates over range(GRID_SIZE) to render three rows and three columns.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players alternate placing X and O
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.TicTacToe.switch_player toggles self.current_player between 'X' and 'O' after each successful make_move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Allow two players to take turns via mouse clicks
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.GameGUI.on_click maps a mouse click to a board cell (get_cell_from_mouse) and calls self.game.make_move(row, col).
game_logic.TicTacToe.check_winner checks rows, columns and diagonals; get_winning_line returns the winning coordinates.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect draw when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.TicTacToe.is_board_full returns True when all cells are occupied; make_move sets game_over when this occurs.
gui.GameGUI.draw_status creates a text element showing the current player, winner, or draw message.
gui.GameGUI.get_winning_cells uses TicTacToe.get_winning_line and draw_board fills those cells with COLOR_WIN_CELL.
gui.GameGUI.on_click resets the game when the restart button area is clicked; on_restart_key resets on 'R' key; draw_restart_button renders the button.
gui.GameGUI.on_motion tracks mouse position; draw_board uses COLOR_HOVER for empty cells under the cursor.
game_logic.TicTacToe.board is a 3×3 list of strings updated by make_move.

judge.summary: The submitted code provides a complete, functional Tic‑Tac‑Toe implementation. The core game logic (board, turn management, win/draw detection, reset) is fully realized in `game_logic.py`. A Tkinter GUI (`gui.py`) renders a 3×3 grid, handles mouse clicks and keyboard input, shows turn/status messages, highlights the winning line, offers hover feedback, and includes a restart button. The entry point `main.py` launches the GUI. All required features are present and there are no evident blockers to execution on a standard Python installation with Tkinter, resulting in a passing verdict.
